ov: A toothed whale of the Arctic, closely related to the beluga. Males have a spiralled tusk 1.5–3 m long, an overgrown left canine tooth.

why.et: The Inuit have hunted narwhals for meat and ivory for thousands of years, and still do under regulation.

cf.tip: Narwhals and belugas are close relatives, similarly built and known to interbreed; only the narwhal has a tusk.

fx: Narwhals spend long periods at great depths.
notes: The existing fact is mostly confirmed: the tusk is the left tooth with "millions of nerve endings". The article doesn’t say ten million. Suggested wording: "The tusk is an overgrown left tooth, packed with millions of nerve endings." No why.et: the source doesn’t mention it being eaten. RESOLVED (owner: approve all): fact rewritten as suggested.
